history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this CSV row is a confirmed duplicate of seq 1192 (id kankalitala-temple-birbhum) — same temple, same town, same district. Kept as a separate file per spec with a -duplicate id. One of the 51 Shakti Peethas: Sati's waist (kankal) is believed to have fallen here, creating a depression that filled with water to form the sacred Kali Kund — the pond itself is the original object of worship. There is no stone/metal/clay idol; a framed painting of Kali standing on Shiva is tended by purohits, and stone fragments believed to be Sati's body parts lie in the kund (raised for worship about every 20 years). The Tantrachudamani lists it as the 28th sati peeth (Devgarbha; Bhairava Ruru); the kund is said to connect underground to Kashi's Manikarnika Ghat. A major centre of gupta (secret) Shakti worship in Bengal.

name: Kankalitala Temple
town_description: Kankalitala is a small temple town in the Bolpur-Sriniketan block of Birbhum district, on the banks of the Kopai river about 10 km north-east of Bolpur/Santiniketan — a quiet, tree-shaded pilgrimage spot famous for its holy pond, visited by most Santiniketan tourists.
